t:
Subchapter A of chapter VII (21 U.S.C. 371 et seq.) is amended by inserting after section 713 the following new section:“SEC. 714. STREAMLINED HIRING AUTHORITY.“(a) In General.—In addition to any other personnel authorities under other provisions of law, the Secretary may, without regard to the provisions of title 5, United States Code, governing 
appointments in the competitive service, appoint employees to positions in the Food and Drug Administration to perform, administer, or support activities described in subsection (b), if the Secretary determines that such appointments are needed to achieve the objectives specified in subsection (c).“(b) Activities Described.—The activities described in this subsection are activities under this Act related to the process for the review of device applications (as defined in section 737(8)).“(c) Objectives Specified.—The objectives specified in this subsection are with respect to the activities under subsection (b), the goals referred to in section 738A(a)(1).“(d) Internal Controls.—The Secretary shall institute appropriate internal controls for appointments under this section.“(e) Sunset.—The authority to appoint employees under this section shall terminate on the date that is 3 years after the date of enactment of this section.”
.

fable.w: This section gives the Secretary streamlined authority to hire federal employees at the FDA, subject to internal controls and a sunset date. The tempting reading is that "appoint" or the reference to device-review goals signals an outside body or stakeholder process, but the appointees are federal employees and no state, industry, expert or public party is consulted on any federal decision. It also contains no rulemaking, hearing, comment period or right to sue.
fable.s: appoint employees to positions in the Food and Drug Administration to perform, administer, or support activities described in subsection (b)

qwen_block.w: This section grants the Secretary of Health and Human Services the authority to hire federal employees for the Food and Drug Administration. The actors involved are the Secretary (federal official) and the employees (federal workers). There is no consultation, coordination, or participation required from parties outside the federal government, such as the public, states, or private entities. Hiring internal staff is an internal administrative action, not public participation.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary may, without regard to the provisions of title 5, United States Code, governing appointments in the competitive service, appoint employees to positions in the Food and Drug Administration

opus.w: This section gives the Secretary faster hiring authority for FDA employees and requires internal controls. It names no outside party (state, expert, company or member of the public) who must be consulted, and it creates no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue. The mention of "device applications" doesn't change this: applications are not participation, and the people hired would be federal employees doing their jobs.
opus.s:
the Secretary may, without regard to the provisions of title 5, United States Code, governing 
appointments in the competitive service, appoint employees to positions in the Food and Drug Administration
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "device applications" points to outside parties dealing with the agency. That fails here: the section only lets the Secretary hire FDA staff to work on reviewing those applications. Applications don't count as participation, and the only other step is the Secretary setting up internal controls, which stays inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section grants the Secretary authority to hire federal employees for the Food and Drug Administration. Hiring employees is an internal administrative action within the federal government. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or decision-making input from parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities). Therefore, it does not constitute participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary may, without regard to the provisions of title 5, United States Code, governing appointments in the competitive service, appoint employees to positions in the Food and Drug Administration
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it involves hiring people, which might imply bringing in outside experts.
Resolution: The text explicitly states that the Secretary may appoint employees "without regard to the provisions of title 5... governing appointments in the competitive service." These are federal employees being hired by a federal agency. Hiring federal employees is an internal personnel matter, not participation by outside parties in a decision-making process.
